meta.description: Run remote BLAST searches against NCBI servers using Biopython Bio.Blast.NCBIWWW. Use when identifying unknown sequences, finding homologs, picking the correct BLAST program (blastn/blastp/blastx/tblastn/tblastx/psiblast/megablast/dc-megablast), interpreting Karlin-Altschul E-values, avoiding the max_target_seqs trap (Shah 2019), choosing composition-based statistics, or limiting searches by organism. Covers RID lifecycle, database choice (nt/nr/refseq_select/swissprot), word-size and CBS taxonomy.

scientific_integrity.detail: All citations (Karlin & Altschul 1990, Altschul et al. 1990/1997, Yu et al. 2006, Shah et al. 2019, Camacho et al. 2009) are real, correctly attributed papers; no fabricated DOIs/PMIDs/statistics anywhere in SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, or the 7 test outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure bioinformatics database-query tool; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or clinical claims in scope or in any output.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled statistical fallacy found. The one overstated claim (megablast 'zero hits' on cross-species query, input 5) is an imprecise symptom description, not a correlation/causation or model-inversion error, and is captured as a P2 finding instead.

code_usability.detail: 2 of 7 documented code patterns (short-peptide PAM30 search, input 3; megablast invocation, input 5) fail exactly as written against the live NCBI API. Both are incorrect-parameter/incorrect-API-contract bugs (NCBI-side ValueError), not syntax errors, infinite loops, or missing dependencies -- the literal M4 trigger conditions -- and both have a confirmed one-line fix. The Skill's primary, most-used patterns (canonical blastn, organism-filtered blastp, XML save/parse, hit filtering) all ran unmodified and correctly. Treated as P1 findings, not a veto, consistent with how equivalent runtime API-contract bugs were handled in the sibling entrez-search/entrez-fetch audits.

functional_suitability.note: Covers the full promised scope (program/db choice, E-value math, CBS, max_target_seqs, RID lifecycle, failure modes) with clear, complete instructions (4/4 completeness). Correctness docked to 2/4: the megablast/dc-megablast program-value guidance and the PAM30 short-peptide code pattern both fail against the live API exactly as documented. Approach is well-matched to the stated one-off/few-sequence identification task (4/4 appropriateness).

reliability.note: A genuinely strong Failure Modes section (6 documented failure modes with trigger/mechanism/symptom/fix) and a Common Errors table give an agent real guidance, but none of it is demonstrated as executable error-handling code (no try/except in any of the 3 example scripts), and the specific NCBI validation errors hit in this audit (PAM30 gap-cost rejection, invalid megablast program string) are not covered by that table.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is a single ~300-line file (under the 500-line guideline) with usage-guide.md and examples/ kept separate; workflow is linear (choose program -> choose db -> submit -> parse -> filter) with no redundant round-trips.

agent_usability.note: Excellent proactive error-prevention (max_target_seqs trap with citation, megablast cross-species misuse called out, CBS defaults explained, nt/nr reproducibility loss flagged repeatedly) and fully consistent terminology between prose and code. Feedback design slightly under-specified -- no explicit output-format contract beyond what the example print() statements show.

human_usability.note: Description and Quick Start prompts use natural researcher phrasing a real user would type. Forgiveness scored down slightly: the Skill anticipates the 'empty FASTA defline' input slip but not the 'program=megablast'/'matrix=PAM30 without gapcosts' slips its own tables would lead an agent into.

security.note: No credentials of any kind (remote BLAST is unauthenticated), no eval/exec of user strings, sequences pass through Biopython's own request-building code to a public NCBI CGI endpoint, no sensitive-data handling anywhere in scope.

maintainability.note: SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, and 3 examples/ are cleanly separated by purpose, but there is no references/ directory at all despite genuinely deep quantitative content (Karlin-Altschul statistics, CBS mode math) that would otherwise be a good progressive-disclosure candidate; the 3 example scripts are directly re-runnable and gave verifiable output.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger scope with an explicit Related Skills section that hands off cleanly to local-blast/remote-homology/ortholog-inference/entrez-fetch. Non-idempotency against nt/nr is disclosed rather than hidden (the T3 determinism consideration for this Skill). Progressive disclosure docked 1 point for the missing references/ split noted above.

inputs.label: BLAST a 12-aa proteomics peptide (short-query parameters)
inputs.note: SKILL.md's 'Short peptide search' pattern (matrix_name=PAM30, word_size=2, CBS=3, no gapcosts) fails on first call: NCBI ValueError 'Gap existence and extension values of 11 and 1 not supported for PAM30'. Root cause: default gap costs are BLOSUM62's 11,1; PAM30 needs 9,1 per SKILL.md's OWN word-size table two sections earlier, but the runnable code block never sets gapcosts. Adding gapcosts='9 1' fixes it (confirmed live: 100 hits, correct self-family matches at E~2-7, consistent with the Skill's own note that short queries need permissive E cutoffs).

key_strengths: Explicit, correctly-cited misuse warnings (max_target_seqs early-termination trap, Shah et al. 2019) head off one of the most common published-workflow BLAST errors.
Canonical and organism-filtered protein search patterns ran unmodified against live NCBI and reproduced textbook-correct top hits (self-matches at 100% identity).
Accurate Karlin-Altschul E-value math with the correct, well-explained guidance to compare bit-scores rather than E-values across databases.
Strong, explicit scope discipline: hands off to local-blast/remote-homology/ortholog-inference for >50 sequences or deep remote homology via a named Related Skills section.
Discloses rather than hides the nt/nr non-determinism/non-reproducibility tradeoff, with a concrete mitigation (refseq_select, snapshot dating).

recommendations.title: megablast/dc-megablast are not valid NCBIWWW.qblast() program values
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's Program decision table and Failure Modes section treat 'megablast' and 'dc-megablast' as program= values; passing either to NCBIWWW.qblast() raises an immediate ValueError. No code pattern anywhere in the Skill shows the real invocation (program='blastn', megablast=True, plus template_type/template_length for dc-megablast).
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's decision table was written at the BLAST+ CLI's conceptual level (where -task megablast is a first-class program choice) without checking that Biopython's remote qblast() API models megablast as a boolean flag on blastn instead.
recommendations.fix: Add a 'Requesting megablast/dc-megablast via qblast()' code pattern showing program='blastn', megablast=True (and template_type='coding'/'optimal', template_length=16|18|21 for dc-megablast), and correct the Program table's program column note to point at it instead of implying program='megablast' is callable directly.

recommendations.title: Short-peptide PAM30 code pattern crashes: missing gapcosts
recommendations.problem: The 'Short peptide search' reference code (matrix_name='PAM30', word_size=2, CBS=3) omits gapcosts; NCBI defaults to BLOSUM62's gap costs (11,1), which PAM30 does not support, and the call fails immediately.
recommendations.root_cause: The word-size/gap-cost table earlier in the same SKILL.md correctly lists PAM30's required gap costs as 9,1, but that value was never carried into the executable code block below it.
recommendations.fix: Add gapcosts='9 1' to the short-peptide qblast() call so it matches the Skill's own word-size table, and add this exact NCBI error string to the Common Errors table so an agent that hits it elsewhere can self-diagnose.

recommendations.title: Megablast cross-species 'zero hits' symptom is overstated
recommendations.problem: Failure Modes claims megablast on a cross-species query produces 'zero hits or only hits to the same species'; a live test on a real 92-nt cross-species query found megablast still returned 2 of 3 species (missing only the most diverged, rat), not zero.
recommendations.root_cause: The symptom description was likely written from the mechanism (28-nt exact-match seeding) rather than validated against a real query where enough by-chance 28-mers still matched a moderately diverged ortholog.
recommendations.fix: Soften the claimed symptom to 'reduced or missing cross-species hits, worse for more diverged sequences' and keep the mechanism explanation, which is accurate.

recommendations.title: Deflineless-sequence behavior may hang rather than return record.query=None
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md documents submitting a bare sequence (no '>id' line) as producing hits with record.query=None. A live test instead did not return within 20+ minutes (vs 61s for the same query with a defline). Root cause unconfirmed -- may be Skill-attributable or an artifact of NCBI/machine load at test time.
recommendations.root_cause: Unconfirmed; needs a clean, isolated re-test to separate Biopython/NCBI defline handling from unrelated load on the audit machine.
recommendations.fix: Re-run this specific case in isolation; if it reproduces, document a client-side timeout/retry wrapper around qblast() for deflineless input rather than relying on NCBI to fail fast.

recommendations.title: No references/ directory despite deep quantitative content
recommendations.problem: Karlin-Altschul statistics and composition-based-statistics mode selection are nontrivial quantitative content living entirely inline in SKILL.md, with no references/ split.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill was authored as a single self-contained file rather than following the progressive-disclosure pattern used elsewhere in this corpus.
recommendations.fix: Move the E-value derivation and CBS mode table into a references/statistics.md, leaving SKILL.md with the decision tables and pointers -- optional, not blocking.
